system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
The Seller’s “standard/cleared” labels are negotiating positions, not agreed terms. The Buyer should review the full package against the AUD 24 million debt-free/cash-free deal, including the specific disclosures and underlying diligence.

| Issue | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation / reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% of price (AUD 4.8m)**. | A materially higher general cap, ideally **100% of price**, or a negotiated amount that reflects the warranties and diligence risks. | **Reject 20%; seek a substantial increase**—AUD 4.8m may not adequately protect against significant undisclosed liabilities. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 tipping basket, with only the excess recoverable. | Lower thresholds, and a **tipping basket** once crossed so recoverable loss is not reduced by the basket; exclude specific indemnities and fundamental claims. | **Reduce the thresholds and make the basket tipping**—the proposed deductible structure leaves the Buyer bearing the first AUD 250,000 plus smaller claims. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | Notify general Warranty Claims within 18 months; Seller proposes all Claim limits apply unless expressly stated otherwise. | A longer period for general warranties (for example, 2–3 years), with separate longer periods for tax, fundamental/title and specific indemnity claims; clear survival and notice mechanics. | **Extend and separate the periods**—18 months may be too short to discover latent issues, and a blanket default risks cutting down other claim types. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to the general cap and time limits. | Separate, materially higher cap (ideally price-level or uncapped) and longer survival for title and capacity; no general basket or de minimis. | **Reject the general regime for fundamental/title claims**—these go to whether the Seller can transfer the agreed shares at all. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims; no express fraud carve-out is stated. | Expressly exclude fraud and fraudulent misrepresentation (including relevant conduct of the Seller and its representatives) from caps, time limits, thresholds, exclusive remedy and non-reliance protections, to the extent legally permissible. | **Add an express carve-out**—the Seller should not obtain contractual protection for its own fraud. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of the data room (DD-002 to DD-012), Accounts, registers and public records; specific disclosures also apply. | Require fair, specific and sufficiently detailed disclosure against the relevant warranty; no blanket data-room or public-register disclosure, and no disclosure that merely points to a document without explaining the issue. | **Reject blanket general disclosure; retain only specific, fairly disclosed matters**—the broad wording may neutralise warranties without identifying what is being qualified. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known to Buyer or advisers, including matters discoverable in the data room or public records. | Limit any exclusion to actual, specific knowledge of identified Buyer personnel, without constructive or imputed knowledge, and preserve claims for fraud and specific indemnities. | **Delete the broad qualifier or tightly narrow it**—mere discoverability is not a fair substitute for the Seller’s warranties. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Seller uses reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent. Disclosure says final consent and evidence of associated conditions are absent. | A condition precedent requiring valid written consent **and satisfaction/waiver of all clause 11.3 conditions**, with a termination right or agreed remedy if not obtained by the long-stop date. | **Make compliant consent and condition satisfaction a completion condition**—Bluefen represents about 30% of FY26 revenue and the draft does not establish that the conditions are met. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | About AUD 3.2m outstanding; release to follow Completion. Disclosure confirms it is unpaid and no final security discharge is included. | Repayment or refinancing at or before Completion, lender payout evidence, and effective release/discharge of all security as a completion deliverable; ensure debt is excluded from equity value under debt-free/cash-free mechanics. | **Do not accept a post-Completion release promise**—the Buyer should not take the Company with outstanding debt or lingering security. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 conditional bonuses are not separately itemised in the funds flow; payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs are unstated. | Reconcile the bonus liability and all associated on-costs; treat them as transaction expenses or debt-like items deducted from proceeds, with payment/withholding and evidence addressed at Completion. | **Require a complete funds-flow adjustment**—the stated price mechanics should not leave the Company or Buyer bearing an undisclosed seller-period bonus cost. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Existing indemnity is limited to the specific SOW3 payment; DD-004 says materials transfer only after every SOW3 fee is cleared, while DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open and no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment. | A specific indemnity covering non-payment, failure to transfer/assign, infringement and associated loss; require cleared payment and effective assignment of all relevant project materials/IP by Completion. | **Expand the indemnity and make transfer a completion deliverable**—the disclosure leaves both the outstanding fee and ownership of important materials unresolved. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Described as preliminary and not expected to be material; no specific remediation or indemnity is offered. DD-006 records a link sent to an unintended external email and possible exposure of about 1,240 records, with access and notification status unknown. | Complete investigation and containment before Completion; obtain relevant incident records and regulatory/privacy advice; require a specific indemnity for incident-related claims, costs and remediation, plus appropriate disclosure and cooperation covenants. | **Do not dismiss it as immaterial; seek targeted protection**—the facts are unresolved and may create privacy, regulatory, customer and remediation exposure. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three renewals totalling AUD 330,000 are characterised as ordinary-course operating costs. Disclosure does not establish whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. | Review the contracts and timing; determine committed and accrued liabilities and whether they are ordinary course; capture any relevant amount in working capital/debt-like adjustments or a specific protection if appropriate. | **Do not accept the characterisation without evidence**—the disclosure does not establish the financial or contractual status of the renewals. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Seller says limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims; also proposes general disclosure and general limitation treatment across claims. | Separate general warranty, fundamental/title, tax, specific indemnity, covenant/debt-like and fraud claims, with tailored caps, periods, thresholds and remedies; expressly state which limitations apply to each category. | **Require an express category-by-category regime**—a blanket clause may unintentionally subject negotiated protections to general warranty restrictions. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Seller relies on DD-012 share register as evidence it holds 100% of the shares. | Verify the register against the constitution, ASIC records, share certificates and any options, liens or other equity rights; obtain title and capacity warranties and delivery of properly executed transfer documents at Completion. | **Treat the register as evidence, not conclusive verification**—the Buyer needs to confirm clean legal and beneficial title and an effective transfer. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Seller considers tax and IP warranties settled under the general regime, without setting out tailored terms. | Negotiate express tax and IP warranty scope, separate caps and survival periods, and specific treatment of known Ironquay risks; ensure tax claims have adequate time for assessment and challenge periods. | **Do not accept “settled” without operative terms**—the Seller’s general regime does not specify the protections or claim periods the Buyer needs for tax and IP exposure. |

These are commercial issue-spotting recommendations based on the supplied summary and disclosure letter. The final drafting should be checked against the complete SPA, schedules, funds flow and underlying diligence documents.
=== END ADVICE ===
